items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: And had a trumpet player -- I forget his last name. Oscar, I know.

ctx.x: So this man Billy Fowell, he just had come back from

Monte Carlo. A lot of people going various places, so he had come back from Monte Carlo and he was organizing a band. I was in the band, and we had violins, singers, and everyone singing (inaudible). And had a trumpet player -- I forget his last name. Oscar, I know. And I always liked to play with people, and he liked me. I was hauling that man, (inaudible) and now thinking that that man hadn't liked me, I had to stop that immediate because he was very, very conservative, man. You know, it was a dance band and…

Well, then, this is my first feeling of a big band with pro's, everybody was a pro. You have records behind/I played so and so, I played here and there. The fellow on the guitar, his name was Edward Gibbs. He was young, we were all sort of younger people. The key men were older people. And Henry Walton, I learned so much from him. Wisdom.
